content: In France, public hospitals provide full coverage for prenatal and postnatal healthcare through the national social security system. Employed women are granted 16 weeks of maternity leave, with daily payments that vary from approximately €9.29 to €84.90 depending on their prior earnings. Financially, pregnancy and the immediate postpartum period do not worsen a family’s economic situation—those facing instability continue to do so, while more affluent families maintain their standard of living. However, practical support for new mothers is notably lacking. Paternity leave is limited to just 11 days—too short to allow mothers adequate time to recuperate physically. As a result, new mothers must juggle constant caregiving responsibilities while still recovering. Securing reliable childcare is another challenge, particularly in and around Paris, where state-run options are scarce. Although subsidized daycare can cost as little as €1,000 annually for lower-income families, availability is extremely limited—one spot exists for every eight children—prompting many families to rely on private alternatives like nannies or in-home care. Any other questions?
